paper_metadata.title: Predictors of early recurrent seizure after first seizure presentation to an emergency service: A retrospective cohort study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the setting and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it is a retrospective review of patients admitted for at least 48 hours, which may introduce selection bias by excluding patients with first seizures who were discharged directly from the ED. Additionally, a significant number of patients (171) were excluded due to lack of follow-up, which may affect representativeness.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: patients aged ≥15 years who presented to the ED of our institutional hospital with FS from January 2001 to December 2014, and were admitted for at least 48 h for clinical observation after initial treatment.
items.reasoning: The authors define the age, clinical setting, and specific timeframe clearly.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We retrospectively reviewed the demographic and clinical data of patients... admitted for at least 48 h
items.reasoning: While the identification method is clear, the requirement for 48h admission creates a potential selection bias toward more severe cases, and the retrospective nature relies on existing records.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: from January 2001 to December 2014
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: the ED of our institutional hospital... a 900-bed, medical teaching university hospital, and the single tertiary-level medical center in southern Thailand.
items.reasoning: The setting and geographic context are well-defined.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: We excluded cases with a known history of epilepsy and all epilepsy mimics (e.g. syncope, transient ischemic attack, psychogenic non-epileptic seizure, and extrapyramidal movement disorders) following consensus of our neurologist team.
items.reasoning: Criteria for exclusion and the definition of 'first seizure' are clearly provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: 171 (13.7 %) patients who did not complete their follow-up evaluations after ED discharge, and 63 (5.0 %) cases with incomplete data records
items.reasoning: Nearly 20% of the potentially eligible FS patients were excluded due to follow-up or data issues, which may bias the sample.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 Demographic data and clinical characteristics of first seizure patients
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive list of age, gender, seizure type, etiology, and comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a significant loss of the initial sample (13.7% lost to follow-up and 5% incomplete data). The study does not provide a comparison of baseline characteristics between those who completed follow-up and those who did not, making it difficult to rule out attrition bias.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: 414 (33.2%) cases were subsequently eligible for statistical analysis... 171 (13.7 %) patients who did not complete their follow-up evaluations
items.reasoning: While 414 is a decent sample size, the loss of 171 patients to follow-up is substantial for a prognosis study.

items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not describe any attempts to contact or retrieve data for the 171 patients lost to follow-up.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 171 (13.7 %) patients who did not complete their follow-up evaluations after ED discharge
items.reasoning: The paper states they did not complete follow-up but does not explain why (e.g., moved, died, seizure-free).

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (etiology, onset time, AED use) are clearly defined and measured using standard clinical and radiological methods. The use of a neurologist consensus for classification adds to the reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Daytime onset seizure (DOS) is a seizure that took place during the daytime, while nocturnal onset seizure (NOS) is one that occurred during sleep at night... acute symptomatic seizure (ASS)... remote symptomatic seizure (RSS)... cryptogenic seizure (CGS)
items.reasoning: The authors provide explicit definitions for the primary prognostic factors.

items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: following consensus of our neurologist team... brain imaging studies (computed tomographic [CT] scan or magnetic resonance image [MRI] of the brain as available)
items.reasoning: Classifications were made by specialists using objective imaging data.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients aged ≥ 65 years were classified as "elderly".
items.reasoning: The age cut-off is a standard clinical definition for elderly populations.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Demographic data, clinical characteristics of the FS, associated comorbidities, and the results of initial investigations at the ED were collected for the study.
items.reasoning: All data were collected from the same ED/hospital records using a standardized retrospective review.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 63 (5.0 %) cases with incomplete data records
items.reasoning: Only 5% of cases were excluded for incomplete data, which is acceptable.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: 63 (5.0 %) cases with incomplete data records [excluded]
items.reasoning: The study used complete case analysis and excluded those with missing data rather than using imputation.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) is clearly defined, but its measurement relies on outpatient follow-up and patient/relative reporting, which is susceptible to recall bias and may miss minor events. There is no mention of blinding the outcome assessors to the prognostic factors.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Recurrent seizure (RS) is a second seizure that occurred more than 24 h after the FS had been successfully treated.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined with a temporal requirement.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: followed by a neurologist at the outpatient department until discontinuation from scheduled follow-ups
items.reasoning: While followed by specialists, the outcome is largely based on clinical history/reporting, and there is no mention of blinding.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: they were re-evaluated and followed by a neurologist at the outpatient department
items.reasoning: The follow-up protocol appears consistent for the analyzed cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to adjust for a wide range of potential confounders, including age, etiology, and AED treatment. The adjustment for 'all demographic and clinical characteristics' is robust.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods (Cox regression) are appropriate for time-to-event data. The authors report both crude and adjusted hazard ratios and provide a clear breakdown of recurrence by time intervals.
